text:
anna: following up on the packaging rfc — i sketched a proposal for a lightweight 'delta entropy' check operators can run before staged activation. goal: catch content-level surprises (token distribution drift, huge vocabulary changes) without needing model eval suites in air-gapped envs

mike: how is this computed offline? air-gapped sites cant call home or run heavy evals

anna: two parts: 1) bundle can optionally include a compact entropy summary: ngram histogram samples, token freq sketch, and embedding centroid stats (if legal). 2) operator shim computes local sample stats on the stored blobs and compares to previous artifact's summary using JS/KL divergence and simple heuristics

sasha: operator shim = responsibility of the k8s operator or a separate sidecar? what actions can it take on an anomaly?

anna: preference is shim inside operator process for tight lifecycle control. actions: fail activation, mark canary fraction to 0, open a quarantined channel, or perform a phased activation with manual approval gate. shim emits signed audit events to local audit log for later review

devon: compute and storage concerns. generating histograms for large models could be heavy.

mike: proposal: make summary optional and tiny. default summary is a 1% reservoir sample of tokenizer outputs plus a 256-bin token-frequency sketch. operator can compute a delta summary from blob bytes using streaming tokenization; we avoid full model runs

anna: exact heuristics i proposed in rfc draft: 
- compute JS divergence of token-frequency sketch between candidate and active version 
- compute embedding-centroid cosine distance if embeddings supplied (optional) 
- compute delta in top-k token mass (e.g., top 100 tokens) 
- compute file-level metadata jumps (size, file-count, new extension types) as coarse signals
threshold examples: JS > 0.12 or centroid-dist > 0.08 triggers soft-fail requiring operator review. these are tunable

sasha: are we comfortable putting any of this summary in the bundle manifest? could leak PII or proprietary prompts if not careful

anna: manifest field should be minimal and hashed where possible. we can store sketches not raw tokens. also include a signed 'summary-hash' so operator verifies integrity. explicitly forbid raw prompt excerpts in the summary

devon: upgrade UX question: if operator soft-fails but team approves, how do we record that approval so that future upgrades dont re-block?

mike: shim writes a signed activation marker to the cluster's sealed store (encrypted, KMS-wrapped) with metadata: bundle-id, summary-hash, approver, rationale, and timestamp. future installs compare marker version to avoid repeated blocks

anna: here's a tiny manifest snippet i mocked (pseudo):

```
manifest: {
  bundle_id: delta-2026-03-01,
  artifacts: [...],
  entropy_summary: {
    token_sketch_b64: <base64-sketch>,
    centroid_hash_b64: <hash>,
    sample_size: 100000
  },
  summary_signature: <sig>
}
```

sasha: that looks fine. suggest an additional operator API: /operator/v1/approve-entropy with POST body {bundle_id, approver, rationale, marker_sig} so we have a single call pattern across distros

devon: if sites disallow any manifest extras for policy, operator-only mode must be supported: operator computes summary locally and compares to stored active summary. so manifest optionality is key

anna: agreed. default flow: if manifest has entropy_summary -> operator verifies signature and runs fast divergence checks. if no summary -> operator runs local sampling then runs checks. either way we avoid calling external services

mike: rollout pattern: canary 1% -> monitor local perf + quality metrics -> 10% -> full. shim supports fractional activations with a sticky marker so rollbacks are predictable

deploy-bot: deploy-check: entropy-summary present: true. js_divergence_est: 0.18 -> result: soft-fail. action: hold activation pending manual approval. :warning:

anna: action items: 1) add entropy_summary optional schema to manifest rfc, 2) define operator shim API and marker format, 3) add default threshold table and telemetry events, 4) write airgap-friendly sample generator tool (go/python)

mike: i'll take item 2 and the approve API sketch

sasha: i'll draft the manifest schema update and the privacy guidelines for summaries

devon: i'll prototype a streaming tokenizer sampler to keep memory bounded

anna: thanks all. i'll update the RFC with these concrete changes and push a follow-up diff this week :thumbsup:
